Here is the U.S. **Core Inflation Rate (YoY%)** from January 2015 to December 2016:

> Core CPI excludes food and energy prices.

| Month | 2015 (%) | 2016 (%) |
|-------------|----------|----------|
| January | 1.6 | 2.2 |
| February | 1.7 | 2.3 |
| March | 1.8 | 2.2 |
| April | 1.8 | 2.1 |
| May | 1.7 | 2.2 |
| June | 1.8 | 2.3 |
| July | 1.8 | 2.2 |
| August | 1.8 | 2.3 |
| September | 1.9 | 2.2 |
| October | 1.9 | 2.1 |
| November | 2.0 | 2.1 |
| December | 2.1 | 2.2 |

### Key Takeaways:
- Core inflation **gradually rose** throughout 2015, starting at **1.6%** and ending at **2.1%**
- In 2016, core inflation **stabilized** around the Fed's **2% target**, ranging between **2.1% and 2.3%**
- The period reflected a **steady tightening labor market** and moderate price pressures

> ⚠️ Please verify these figures with official sources such as the **U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)** at bls.gov.
